notes.title: Empire of Ember goes to FULL RELEASE TODAY!!!
notes.notes:
Lightbringers!

The wait is finally over!!! We're thrilled to announce that Empire of Ember has left Early Access today and is now fully released on Steam!

Since the game went into Early Access on March 30th 2021, we've been working tirelessly on new features and content, revamped graphics and dialogues, localizations, and a long list of other gameplay improvements  – as well as completing the main storyline and single-player campaign. 

During all this time, and thoughout the whole development process, the game has grown and evolved thanks to all your support and feedback, and we would never be able to thank you enough!

To celebrate this important day, Empire of Ember is releasing with a special launch discount of 25%, which will last until Jan 27th. Also, we've created this amazing release trailer you can check out in our YouTube channel!

Become a battlemage and wield magic and sword in this epic tale. 

The destiny of an empire lies in your hands!

notes.title: Dev Blog #19 - Last content update before full release!
notes.notes:
Hi there, Lightbringers! 

It’s been some time since the last dev blog, but we haven’t been idle at Poleaxe Games, and, as the end of the last milestone approached, we’ve been working tirelessly to finish the last level of the game.

And finally... after almost four years in development and eight months on Early Access, we’re proud to announce that we’ve implemented the LAST UPDATE that completes the main storyline of Empire of Ember! HURRAAAY!!! 🥳🎉🎉🎉

In this last level, our Lightbringer hero will at last confront the forces that endanger the world in a final battle... but we don’t want major spoilers, so we’re only leaving you this image 😉

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39590227/cc0104da414808fad9c289d815edf508dcb3f2da.jpg

So these are the exciting news we wanted to share with you!!! 

Now that the game is content complete, we will focus on testing and polishing ahead of the final release of the game. You can follow up our progress with the final touches on our Discord server, and our Social Media channels, Twitter, Facebook and Reddit.

As always, thank you all for your feedback on the game! If you haven’t already, please remember to leave us a review on Steam, update your old review, or rate existing reviews that you think would be useful for other users.

Also, wishlist and follow Empire of Ember on Steam, and spread the news 😊

Have a great week!

notes.title: New player introduction patch
notes.notes:
Enemy lairs and hordes close to your base now have far fewer enemies, while those far away have slightly more. This gives the player easier fight options if they need it.
 At the start of the game, you will encounter roaming pitchfork farmer hordes in addition to the other horde types (such as goblins) since peasants are pretty easy to mow down. However, they give less gold per kill.
 Pitchfork farmers now do much more damage, attack more often, and have slightly more health allowing them to be more useful at low levels. This way if the player wipes out it is easier to recover, and also makes them viable combat units and not just fodder.
 Player starts with more population at the start of the game, so new players can withstand a few losses without running out.
 Higher level units take half as much steel to recruit or upgrade to. This lets the player recover strong armies or individually lost units more easily. It was so expensive before high level units still cost a lot to purchase directly.
 Player starts with a larger starting army limit. This reduces difficulty for new players by reducing player aggro, without affecting end-game difficulty.
 The player now does slightly less melee damage to account for the greater attack speed vs. other weapons. Previously the player was able to kill the majority of enemies by himself.
 Horde and lair battles now give more experience, making an under-leveled player able to grind them and be rewarded even if there are not many enemies.
 Add gameplay tab option to disable screen turning grey at player low health.

notes.title: Dev Blog #9 - The first animation patch for Empire of Ember has been released!
notes.notes:
Hi there, Lightbringers! 

In this week’s dev blog we are pleased to announce that the first animation patch for Empire of Ember has finally been implemented in the game! 

This first pass includes improved first-person animations for the different styles of combat; that is, melee, bow, spell and staff attacks. 

These improvements will be most noticeable during melee combat. This should make the animations feel more responsive, cleaner and balanced than before. The main difference now is that players will need to use their reflexes to block attacks in time, or cancel attacks in progress. Melee users will now be able to block with a magical shield, and also have a new unlockable “shove” ability to counteract enemies that are using shields.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39590227/e0ef932ffb4ff9de51366ff3e43d334c18c4e7c1.gif

Implementing the animations for Empire of Ember hasn’t been a bed of roses all the time, as there have been some very challenging moments. Most issues have been a consequence of the hired animators not properly testing their work in-game. Even animators with 20 years of experience had trouble copying FBX files from Maya to Unity, or would not know how to use an animation controller, for instance.

This has unfortunately slowed down progress. Improving the game’s animation has taken about four times longer than expected, and has been more expensive than originally planned. On the bright side, all the setbacks have given main developer Kevin Jenkins the chance to make other improvements that resulted in a better outcome and thus, a better game.

Further additions to the animations are planned for the future, but as these are not a pressing concern anymore, the developers will focus on other fixes for the moment. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39590227/f43fb2ed998b0a54a118f060b609478dc3cbc324.png

Since the Steam Early Access release in late March, the dev team has been working really hard to polish the weakest parts of the game. All feedback from users has been very useful so far to introduce new features as well as helping fix bugs, so we welcome you all to try the game and let us know how it can be further improved. You can have an impact in shaping Empire of Ember and helping it reach its full potential!

If you would like to help us, please wishlist and follow the game and tell everyone about it! You can also follow our progress by joining our community on Discord, Steam, and our Social Media channels: Twitter, Facebook and Reddit.

See you soon! Take care and have a great week :)

notes.title: Cities patch
notes.notes:
Requested missions available while negative reputation:
1. (High probability) Pay tribute. A high gold price, restoring your reputation by a certain amount.
2. (Low probability) Ransom from the enemy boss. An unusually difficult random map mission spawns nearby, with a captured villager. At the start of the mission you can pay if you have the money and win automatically, otherwise you can just fight. If the villager dies or the mission times out you fail the mission.

Always available while negative reputation
3. Siege (Army): Attempt to destroy the enemy city. Drops reputation greatly. City will respawn with a new ruler at slightly negative status after some time if you win.

Requested missions available while positive reputation:
4. (Common) Recruit units for me. You have some days to train/recruit X of some particular unit you have already unlocked, where X is the cost of the units in resources plus some profit.
5. (Common) I will pay for large quantity X of stone
6. (Common) Defeat enemy patrols: Defeat all within some timeframe. Causes target reputation loss.
7. (Common) Meet informant. Guards start neutral. A villager is in a downloaded city at a random spot. Breaking or killing anything turns everyone hostile. Talking to this villager also turns all guards hostile. After talking to the villager, escape. Killing guards furthers reputation loss.
8. (Common) Insult. Text mission only. Walk to another city and insult their leader. Player can pick from various insults. Causes reputation loss with that city, but gain with the source city.
9. (Common) Show of force. Same as walk around, but killing enemy units gains reputation for the source city, with more reputation loss/gain for the target and source city respectively for more units killed.

Coming next week
10. (Rare) Magic contest: Shoot targets rapidly to get to the next round.
11. (Rare) Archery contest: Bet on how far you can get in the contest. You can't move from your starting spot and start with a cracked bow only. Shoot various targets. Success makes new peasants spawn farther away. You only have a limited number of arrows.
12. (Rare) Arena battle: 10 waves of increasingly difficult battles. Enemies keep spawning until you are knocked out. You can place a bet on how far you can get.
Extra mission available while max reputation
13. Court princess: Player can give all gems currently in inventory to the ruler's daughter. Once you reach a certain gold value of gems she agrees to marry you. Shows 1 of 3 custom illustrations. You can marry all 3 daughters, but can only marry each daughter once. Destroying this city resets the love resource, but does not unmarry you if married already.
Positive reputation benefit
City internally keeps track of a gold value of free units to be provided to the player. Each city has an archetype – melee, ranged, or magic that scales with campaign time. Being married doubles the rate of gold increase. Higher reputation also increases gold increase.

notes.title: Campaign army balance patch

Campaign army balancing overview
Certain units are now more effective against other units. Broadly speaking

 Archers beat unshielded units, and especially mages, if engaged at range. You will still need to direct the archers to fire at the mages in commander mode.
 Shielded units beat archers of the same level

 Skirmisher type units (goblins) beat melee units of the same level but have low health so die easily if caught
 Two handed / high damage units beat units that ressurect or summon other units
 Undead beat non-undead of the same type, however undead cannot be saved through leadership

notes.title: Staff and attribute balancing patch
notes.notes:
Attributes improvement

Previously you could outrun all enemies even at level 1 and dodge several times. You also had enough mana to cast most spells several times and could recharge between battles. Athleticism now is a very important stat defensively, as without it you can only dodge once and can't really outrun enemies. You need to put points into willpower if you plan to use magic more than one or twice. The staff doesn't slow you down when on cooldown anymore, but the cooldown resets if you dodge or run (like a regular shooter reload) so you are now very vulnerable with the staff and can't just tank enemies while dodging. 

While you can still focus on particular stats doing so now makes your character unbalanced and vulnerable. This means there's a tradeoff that wasn't really there before. Also the staff isn't automatically the best weapon, it's good for mid-range but leaves you vulnerable close range

Changelist

[olist]
 Fix DungeonTile_Stairs not spawning enemies
 Fix dungeon boss rooms sometimes not ending due to units on the roof
 All melee attacks can now hit multiple targets, to increase the usefulness of melee attacks as well as reduce frustration from hitting walls

 Reduce slow effect time of mana bolts to 1 seconds. Also show effect when slow effect is active on enemies

 Athleticism improvement: Dodging without improving athleticism now takes nearly all your stamina. Improving athleticism reduces this cost. Running now starts out only 30% faster than walking, but increases as you improve athleticism.
 Improve staff: I found it was not fun to suddenly not be able to move effectively if your staff went on cooldown. This was updated so you can still fully walk. However, running, dodging, jumping, casting spells, or not equipping the staff prevents the staff from recharging while you are doing one of those activities. This also indirectly makes willpower more important, because if you cannot shoot you need to rely on your magic. 
 Improve staff: Mana bolts no longer cause living enemies to flee on damage.  The rate of fire made it too probable to occur and so the player wouldn't need to defend himself other than by shooting attackers.

notes.title: Update 3/6/2021
notes.notes:
[olist]
 On the army recruitment page, you can now select loadouts for certain units that hold weapons. For example, a two handed weapon vs. a sword and shield.
 Enemy and friendly armies on maps that focus on large scale battles now move as a group, in formation
 Friendly units on most maps now start out attacking enemies rather than following the player. This is to reduce the number of commands needed for new players and it is less important to always follow the player now that friendly armies move as a group
 Design change: Previously units only got experience from completing battles while in your army. Now, units left in town now also gain a small amount of experience per day. This provides the player a safe path to level up units while low on gold, by recruiting low level units then leaving them behind. The UI panel title was renamed from Garrison to Training to indicate to the player that leaving units behind gains them experience. Units in the garrison now take half upkeep rounded up, rather than no upkeep as before, to reflect the benefit of training them.
 Design change: Previously it was too random to discover new unit types. This led to the player upgrading his army through normal gameplay to max level, with no apparent further upgrade path. To fix this, unit unlock quests cost gold instead of spellbooks, because the player often does not have spellbooks. Unlocking new unit types through dungeons is now extremely likely to the point that this is the primary way to unlock new unit types. In addition, rewards from dungeon opportunities have better rarity scaling, so you are much less likely to see high-tier objects. This makes researching multiple times more beneficial, and finding a rare object more exciting.
 Design change: Previously upgrading the player's tower cost many of all types of resources. Now it simply takes spellbooks and gold. This makes it more clear early in the game what building a library is for, and to provide a benefit to libraries even if the player has no units to research
 Design change: Using food as upkeep previously felt like just another form of money and was required to field armies, so was a forced decision rather than an interesting one. Converted the concept of food to population. 1 population is used to recruit each unit and units no longer have food upkeep. This makes lower level worthwhile to keep alive, as it costs a population point to recruit both low and high level units, and provides an incentive to directly recruit higher level units.  The major benefit of farms is now to increase your army limit. You can get more population from villages, putting more play emphasis on trading with villages.
 More localization work
 AI fighting other AI will now knock each other down if their attack has knockback ability and also reduces the target to zero poise. This is useful for pitchfork farmers, who are designed to play this role when in large groups.
 Skipped painting terrain from placed buildings on all maps but the player's city, which greatly improves load times and reduces memory usage for those maps that no longer do so.
 Skipped removing trees from terrain when trees intersected spawning AI. This turned out to be an extremely slow operation so I'm just not doing it for now. I might revisit later if it is a problem.
 Moved when the AI's behavior tree is loaded, removing the hitch that occurred when the goblins spawn in the first city defense mission.
 The player's movement is reduced when the staff charge is depleted and recharging, not only while attempting to fire. This fixes the exploit of being able to kite enemies with impunity, and adds strategy as to when to fully deplete the staff vs. holding fire.
 Friendly villages are now more likely to spawn closer to the player's tower. Previously they would spawn at entirely random locations within the biome, making them too hard to find.
 In-air blood decals from minor damage to humans are now larger
 Units that are holding large shields now attack and move more slowly. Regular sized shields only have a small movement penalty.
 Units that are using blunt weapons do about 85% damage to all unit types. Units that are using slash weapons do 100% weapons to living units, and about 66% damage to undead units. This adds strategy to what loadout the player gives to his units.
 The player's staff attacks now do less damage, to offset that they rarely miss.
 Walls now have 50% more health, to make siege battles last longer
[/olist]

notes.title: Update 3/1/2021
notes.notes:
This update:


 Reduce memory usage by about 4 GB. This was due to a bug in Unity we were able to work around, but in effect the game will load faster and run slightly better
 Greatly improved enemy animations. This had a bigger impact than expected and makes the game a lot more fun and interesting.
 Fix being able to use your weapon in city roam mode
 Player now only attacks in one of 4 directions with equivalent timings for each direction, with fast and power variations
 Fix village producing gold per day
 Fix leadership chance to survive display on level up screen
 Weaponry now also increases your melee swing speed
 The bow can shoot faster but moving while shooting is less accurate. This is to emphasize it is a long-ranged weapon
 Boon of the ancestors quests will now continue rather than repeat forever
 Fix Army Management scrollbar showing when it should not
 Fix randomly generated dungeon showing group quest rather than solo quest
 Player sword now raycasts per frame based on the sword position rather than the screen center. This way the player does not have to swing exactly at the target.
 Abort the swing in a forced recovery state if it hits a shield while not doing a power attack
 Abort the swing if it hits something that doesn't take damage, such as a wall.
 Slow down player attacks but do more damage per attack
 Enemies should not block with bows
 Adjust trap trigger position in dungeon

notes.title: Game Update 2/13/2021
notes.notes:
Vines barrels now do low damage over time in addition to rooting their opponents.
 Equipment you buy or find is now color coded to indicate rarity
 Stamina abilities now cost less to use, but stamina recovers more slowly, to make combat more tactical while also letting players use abilities more often once combat starts
 Increase staff total charge so player is less likely to run out of shots against a single enemy. This is balanced by the time to recharge taking longer between enemies.
 Added beat tutorial achievement as a placeholder for further achievement work
 Removed less helpful autosaves to reduce the number of autosave files. Autosave filenames now also hint at why they were generated.
 Increase unit time to forget units so they can reach from their starting positions across long maps
 Increase starting spellbooks to 20 to match costs for random events
 Increase starting steel to 20 so the player is guaranteed an upgrade option for their first unit upgrade events
 Fixed too high level units being selected for enemy spawns from spawn points, meaning enemies in dungeons were often too high level.
 Fixed pathfinding in dungeons
 The chest in boss rooms in dungeons now gives a good random reward rather than gold

notes.title: Gameplay patch 2/11/2021
notes.notes:
At the end of encounters enemies now have a chance to drop loot of varying rarity. Loot can take the form of gemstones to be sold for money, rings or amulets that increase your stats, or rarely rings or amulets that grant special powers.
 Gold, aside from dropped loot, is now more scarce, and is more scarce overall. This should make the player have to work for money rather be granted enough to buy a building after every fight.
 Food is now dropped from bandit camps, but not every battle
 There are now more enemies in bandit lairs, but fewer enemies in roaming battles. This gives the player more options of what difficulty fights to take up
 Increased volume of avatar footsteps
 The game will no longer make a new autosave immediately after loading a game. This will prevent making multiple of the same autosave when retrying a mission
 All mission levels up to mission 3 are now included in the build
 Fixed attack decision not correctly calculating priority to targets. Most noticeably enemies are now more likely to attack the player if the player is threatening them
 Fix terrain painter making terrain black
 Fix spawning units of the wrong type in downloaded cities
 Fix units looking in the wrong direction in commander mode
 Ranged units with a hold position order whose attacks are blocked will now wait to attack rather than run back and forth

notes.title: Melee Combat Update 2/9/2021
notes.notes: Player melee combat reworked. It now matters which direction you attack in, enemies can block your attacks by direction, and enemies do a better job of blocking and counterattacking.
